# Native combined source setup

Root `install.sh` now coordinates native app/widget setup in both maintained source checkouts and prepared runtime bundles. The package builder copies this one script; its duplicate `resources/setup.sh` and the obsolete Python widget installer are removed. Source widget commands use `bash linux/install-widget.sh`; prepared bundles invoke `bin/mluva-install-widget` directly. Options, terminal confirmation, ownership checks and partial-failure behavior retain the released contract.

Source setup requires the repository-pinned Rust toolchain and a C compiler before starting. The existing widget command builds with `--no-default-features` and an explicit compiler host target, without GLib/SQLite development dependencies. Its ownership preflight runs before system packages or app installation. After confirmation, setup requests native runtime/development packages and uses the existing source app transaction. Prepared bundles request runtime packages only and require neither a compiler nor Python. App-only source setup skips widget preflight, as before; its normal build prerequisites remain documented in [CONTRIBUTING](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md#local-setup).

The `application` Cargo feature keeps the installer's GLib/SQLite dependencies and related executables/test targets in default builds. The widget-only route uses the same ownership/staging implementation, not a second policy in Bash. `linux/native-source-command.sh` retains compiler process-group cancellation, temporary-bundle cleanup and foreground terminal input for native commands. A source command compiles before invoking the requested native CLI, including help; prepared commands execute directly.

## Independent checks

The immutable reference remains v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. No released expected values were changed. The [thirty actual released setup processes](released-setup.json), SHA-256 `2c2001670581fb608acd3fccbe3415b3fb6e86c9b60f731ad3c70aff59e9cdd4`, now compare against both source and package routes: sixty candidate invocations covering ordered options, private-terminal answers, platform selection, unsupported contexts, preflight ordering and failures at each installation boundary. External package/app/widget endpoints are observable peers; their failures must retain the same status, output and order.

Runtime package comparison retains the previously reviewed removal of Python/GI tooling and addition of OpenSSL/SQLite. Source mode additionally requests the development dependencies listed in [the Linux guide](../../../../linux/README.md#supported-desktop-contract). Their names were checked against primary distribution catalogs, including [Arch pkgconf](https://archlinux.org/packages/core/x86_64/pkgconf/), [Fedora GTK](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/gtk4/gtk4-devel/), [Fontconfig](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/fontconfig/fontconfig-devel/), [OpenSSL](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/openssl/openssl-devel/), [SQLite](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/sqlite/sqlite-devel/), [pkg-config](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/pkgconf/pkgconf-pkg-config/) and [GCC](https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/gcc/gcc/). This observes exact package requests without executing a real package manager or establishing Fedora ABI compatibility.

The existing actual combined-setup owner now runs five workflows against each route: combined setup, app-only setup/removal, widget failure, foreign-widget refusal and package failure. Source cases build the actual optimized executables; prepared cases install the newly assembled native bundle. Native ownership transactions, file copying, rollback, the installed schema validator and public launcher all run. Only package management and shell registration are controlled peers. The ten workflows verify matching app/widget versions and QML bytes, enabled registration, usable app retention after widget failure, refusal before package changes, untouched unrelated user bytes, and installed self-removal. Absolute-path Python traps have positive controls and must remain unused.

`source_widget_staging_builds_without_desktop_development_libraries` builds from an empty target directory, with both Python and pkg-config replaced by positively checked failing commands. It stages the real manifest/QML through the public source wrapper, leaves the private home empty and must never touch either trap. The old root installer first failed at the Python boundary with status 99 (`tmp/native-root-source-before.log`). The initial widget build first failed at pkg-config with status 73 because GLib was still mandatory (`tmp/native-widget-build-before.log`). The optional application dependencies repair that genuine build boundary.

The existing widget comparison runs with `--no-default-features`: **71 released transactions / 98 states** match actual process outcomes, manifests/receipts/QML, modes, Git ownership and rollback. Both additional native ownership faults preserve replacement paths and the previous installation. The fixture SHA-256 remains `9916693a4b16025c88227a092cdfa946476262a5d2f69fc8508ebfec51b9e72c`.

The affected app-only source checks also pass: actual install/upgrade/help/removal, failed and cancelled compiler preservation, and legacy migration through a real private terminal with observable authentication. The actual bundle installed by combined source setup passes resident startup: **38 public states, 13 actions, five CLI contracts**, second-instance forwarding, cold synthetic-PCM Record/quit and three startup faults. The test's microphone wording refers to its synthetic private audio endpoint.

## Removed tests and retained ownership

The complete Python widget implementation, its tests, root-setup tests, callers and relevant installer history were reviewed before deletion. `linux/tests/test_setup.py` contributed eleven cases; `linux/tests/test_install_widget.py` contributed sixteen. Their observable contracts retain stronger independent Rust owners:

| Removed exact test names | Retained coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `test_omarchy_setup_installs_dependencies_app_then_bundled_widget`, `test_app_only_preserves_plugins`, `test_fedora_setup_skips_omarchy`, `test_setup_stops_after_failure`, `test_setup_requires_supported_context` | Thirty frozen released processes compared against both setup routes, plus ten actual source/package workflows, including real private-terminal confirmation and Python-blocked builds/installations. |
| `test_install_and_upgrade_load_new_qml_and_preserve_previous_bundle`, `test_check_is_read_only`, `test_preserve_customized_or_ambiguous_installation` | Existing [widget transactions](README.md) compare staged/installed content, read-only preflight, backups and all ownership/modified/duplicate guards. |
| `test_failed_shell_update_restores_previous_files`, `test_legacy_git_migration_without_network`, `test_wait_for_asynchronous_shell_discovery` | The same independent widget owner retains both shell-failure rollback paths, actual private Git trees, discovery success/timeout and additional promotion/replacement faults. |

No test-only production hook or new framework was introduced. Existing integration owners were extended, with one new fresh-build check for the prerequisite boundary. The frozen release and temporary comparison observers remain outside the final maintained implementation.

## Accepted artifacts and limits

`tmp/native-root-reviewed.log` and `tmp/native-root-reviewed-evidence/session.D7H63G/` retain the complete accepted sequence: optimized bundle/archive construction, all three setup tests, widget transactions without application dependencies, both source-entry checks and resident startup. `setup-actual/source-installed-bundle` and `setup-actual/package-installed-bundle` name the installed private payloads. The archive test independently checks inventory/modes/links, dependency notices, GNU tar extraction, repeated-byte equality, corrupt-cache refusal and preservation of existing destinations.

The optimized main executable SHA-256 remains `472fa8e8503458189b2d62a2cbeed3def052ea0ce0522935ec58c3fe31966aca`. The source-built bundle receipt is `a79177eeccb6224b59c1dc71a84838241a7ba80e32f3b6a31b22e4027e6c6791`; the separately tested package/archive receipt is `6bbf52b413a256777401fceadb8c6d72fdfeeafad16b11d8d6176cf185c5ee58`. Its archive is 17,272,992 bytes and has the same SHA-256 on repeated construction: `dd245c797f40bcea3bf40512a88f01881716882c93714103dadf9fabd9cee46e`. The 240-record dependency inventory remains `77ac24e78a5344e914341c9c40163e196ebdc26558dcd0eeeb1136428c6ced6d`.

Final validation passes **139 Rust tests, zero failures and 64 ignored environment checks across 97 suites**, plus strict all-target Clippy in both default-workspace and widget-only feature configurations. The affected ignored checks were explicitly executed above. Formatting, diff and the documented ShellCheck gate pass, including installer support scripts. The remaining Linux gate passes **571 tests, Ruff and formatting for 164 files**; its existing PyGObject deprecation warning remains. Private-bus shortcut registration, binding and lifecycle pass in `tmp/global-shortcut-portal-smoke/run.kcU7XT/`. Results are retained in `tmp/native-root-final-workspace.log`, `tmp/native-root-final-clippy.log`, `tmp/native-root-final-widget-clippy.log`, `tmp/native-root-final-linux.log` and `tmp/native-root-final-shortcut.log`.

Two harness failures remain visible: `tmp/native-root-final-workspace-long-tmp.log` records an excessively long Unix-socket temporary path; `tmp/native-root-final-linux-x11-harness.log` records headless Python tests inheriting the GUI runner's X11 display and another long pytest socket path. The final runs use short worktree scratch directories and clear display/session-type variables for the headless Python gate. No production code, test expectation or test was weakened to address either harness error.

These are local x86_64 cached builds in disposable display/session/accessibility, network/PID/mount, device and data boundaries. They do not perform package installation, live compositor registration, real authentication or physical input. Fresh-distribution dependency/ABI checks, actual Quickshell hot upgrade, complete joined application/target/theme/scale acceptance, physical keys/microphone, remaining performance measurements and final Python removal stay open. All whole-workflow matrix rows remain Pending; the verified installed 1.6.0 app/widget and user data remain unchanged.
